name: Standard scaled dot-product attention (multi-head, softmax)
aka: SDPA; MHA; vanilla / full / dense attention; 'Attention Is All You Need'

source.title: Attention Is All You Need
source.authors: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin (Google)

firstShipped.model: GPT-1 / BERT (kept SDPA+MHA, swapped sinusoids for learned positions)

problem: RNNs compute one token at a time — 'precludes parallelization within training examples' — and a dependency between distant tokens has to travel O(n) steps. The Transformer's bet: throw the recurrence away and pay for all-pairs attention instead.
idea: softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)·V. Every position scores every other position with a dot product, the scores are scaled by 1/√d_k so softmax does not saturate at large d_k, softmax turns them into weights, and the output is a weighted sum of values. Do it h times in parallel with smaller heads (multi-head) at the cost of one full-width head.
buys: O(1) sequential ops and O(1) maximum path length per layer (Table 1) — everything is a batched matmul, so the base model trains in 12 h on 8 P100s
Multi-head (h=8, d_k=64) costs the same as one big head and single-head is 0.9 BLEU worse (Table 3 A)
Exact: every token can read every other token; the reference quality every mechanism below is measured against
costs: O(n²·d) time and an n×n score matrix per head per layer — the quadratic bill every later mechanism exists to lower
At inference the KV cache grows linearly with context: 2·layers·heads·d_head values per token
'Reduced effective resolution due to averaging' (their words); the sinusoid's extrapolation was only 'may allow' and in practice was weak enough that GPT-1/BERT dropped it

chatbot2k.why: the default — with FlashAttention it is exact and fast

rag32k.why: still fine on modern kernels; KV cache is the thing to watch

coding128k.why: exact is best for recall; the KV cache is what forces GQA/MLA

agent1m.why: 1M² scores per head and a terabyte-scale KV cache — you keep the semantics and change the pattern

pickWhen.verdict: Never wrong, only expensive. Everything on this timeline is somebody looking at this bill and paying less of it.

name: Sinusoidal positional encoding

source.title: Attention Is All You Need, §3.5 Positional Encoding
source.evidence: [v1] Mon, 12 Jun 2017 — §3.5: learned vs sinusoidal 'produced nearly identical results (see Table 3 row (E))'; sinusoids chosen because they 'may allow the model to extrapolate'

problem: No recurrence means position has to be injected somewhere. Learned tables (ConvS2S, a month earlier) work but cap the length. Can a fixed function do the same job and maybe generalise beyond it?
idea: PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos/10000^{2i/d}), PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos(·): each dimension pair is a sinusoid at a geometrically spaced wavelength from 2π to 10000·2π. Because PE(pos+k) is a linear function of PE(pos), relative offsets are in principle learnable.
buys: Zero parameters; defined for any position, so nothing crashes past training length
Quality tied learned positions on WMT (25.7 vs 25.8 BLEU)
The frequency-band idea is exactly what RoPE later turns into a rotation
costs: 'May allow' extrapolation was optimistic: models trained short still degrade past training length because the *model* never saw those inputs, even if the encoding is defined
Adds position to the residual stream, so it leaks into values and every layer, not just the attention score
Absolute in form; the relative structure has to be discovered by the network

rag32k.why: fine at trained length; do not expect free extension

coding128k.why: RoPE + scaling gives you a lever; sinusoids do not

pickWhen.verdict: The right first guess in 2017. It lost to learned positions in GPT/BERT and to RoPE in every decoder after 2021, but its frequency ladder lives on inside RoPE.

name: Local (block) self-attention — Image Transformer

source.title: Image Transformer
source.authors: Parmar, Vaswani, Uszkoreit, Kaiser, Shazeer, Ku, Tran (Google)

problem: 32×32×3 images are 3,072-token sequences; full self-attention was already too expensive eight months after the Transformer.
idea: Restrict each query block to a local 1-D or 2-D neighbourhood of memory blocks — the first local self-attention in a transformer, two years before Longformer named the sliding window.
buys: Attention cost proportional to block size, not sequence length
Kept SOTA image generation at the time
costs: Receptive field grows only with depth; no global tokens

pickWhen.verdict: Lineage: the ancestor of every sliding-window layer, born in vision.

name: Relative position representations (Shaw et al.)
aka: Shaw RPE; relation-aware self-attention; a^K_ij / a^V_ij edge embeddings
problem: Absolute positions (learned or sinusoidal) carry no built-in notion of 'how far apart are i and j', which translation clearly wants. Quality, not cost.
idea: Learn a vector per relative offset (clipped at ±k, k=16) and add it to the key (and optionally the value) inside the attention score: e_ij = x_iW^Q (x_jW^K + a^K_{i−j})ᵀ/√d.
buys: +1.3 BLEU En-De over absolute positions; adding absolute on top gave nothing more
Translation-invariant: the same parameters serve any absolute position
The origin of the whole relative family: Transformer-XL, T5 bias, ALiBi and, in spirit, RoPE
costs: The naive implementation materialises an [n, n, d] tensor per layer — quadratic memory; Music Transformer had to invent 'skewing' to make it linear
Offsets beyond the clip distance are indistinguishable
Cache-unfriendly for incremental decoding compared with bias-only (T5) or rotation-only (RoPE) schemes

chatbot2k.why: fine for short encoders (DeBERTa descends from it)

rag32k.why: the [n,n,d] cost or the clip bites

pickWhen.verdict: The idea won; this implementation lost to cheaper ways of saying the same thing.

name: Music Transformer (relative attention with 'skewing')
oneLiner: First at-scale use of Shaw-style relative attention; the 'skewing' trick reduces its memory from O(n²d) to O(nd).
whyFootnote: An implementation fix for a node already on the timeline.

name: Efficient Attention: Attention with Linear Complexities

source.title: Efficient Attention: Attention with Linear Complexities

oneLiner: Reorders softmax(Q)·(softmax(K)ᵀV) so cost is linear in n — the earliest linear-complexity attention found, in vision, 18 months before 'Transformers are RNNs'.
whyFootnote: Vision-only and did not give the causal/RNN form; the canonical linear-attention launch is Katharopoulos 2020.
